newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA Peugeot stock rises on H1 sales.
newsitem.headline: PSA Peugeot stock rises on H1 sales.

text.p: Shares in carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen surged on Thursday after the company reported a 6.3 percent in first-half sales despite a collapse in the French car market, prompting analysts to raise their recommendations on the stock.
Portfolio managers said Natexis, Paribas Capital Markets, and Credit Lyonnais had raised their ratings following a similar switch last week by Cheuvreux de Virieu.
The stock was up 6.98 percent at 736 francs at 1100 GMT after easing from a year high of 744 francs.

Paribas raised its rating to buy from neutral and said its target for the stock was 800 francs. It expects to raise its earnings per share forecasts, currently at 16.90 francs for 1997 and 31.50 francs for 1998, after the first-half sales rise.

The Peugeot group said the rise was due to strong light commercial vehicle sales and exports outside Europe, which offset weakness in the French market which contracted 24 percent in the first half of 1997 after the expiry of state car buying incentives.

Natexis raised its rating to outperform, or 'B1', from underperform, or 'B3', citing a strong second-quarter performance and the surprising strength of light commercial vehicles, notably the new Citroen Berlingo and Peugeot Partner.
It expects a profit of 515 million francs for this year -- it previously forecast breakeven -- and 2.1 billion for 1998, up from 590 million previously.
Brokerage Ferri kept its rating unchanged but said the company's sales were better than the 4.4 percent rise it expected.

Wargny is more pessimistic, retaining its 'reduce holding' rating on the stock, citing the continuing price war and a deterioration in the Peugeot group's product and geographic mix flagged by the company.
